international.title: NSW halts new law to crack down on underquoting by real estate agents at 11th hour
international.summary: Backdown is one of several premier Chris Minns has announced in recent weeks as state prepares for election in March The Minns government has mothballed laws intended to protect homebuyers from underquoting after the premier said real estate agents in his Sydney electorate had raised concerns about their effect amid a housing market downturn. Changes due to come into effect on Tuesday would have banned agents in New South Wales from lowering the advertised price of a property beneath a written offer previously rejected by a seller, with fines of up to $110,000 or three times an agent’s commission, whichever was greater.
